title: 'Lonely' Brain Waves in Sleep Linked to Weaker Memory
paragraphs: Sleep is good for memory. In sleep, the brain makes waves. These waves move across the brain.
Scientists in California did a study. They compared young adults and older adults. In young people, the waves travel far. In older people, they often travel less.
Some older people had a protein called tau in the front of the brain. They had more short waves. The next day, they remembered fewer words.

questions.q: Which people had waves that travel far?
What did people with short waves remember?
